text: The AI output indicating features that the model associates with glioma is inconclusive and must not be acted upon; the result requires review by a qualified radiologist or specialist physician. Imaging alone cannot establish tumour type, grade, molecular subtype or margins, and the model's uncertainty is high when several classes are possible [nci-cns-pdq-hp]. Clinical and neurological assessment is essential because symptoms depend on tumour location, size and growth rate rather than on tumour type alone [nci-cns-pdq-hp] [ninds-brain-tumors]. Any sudden severe headache, new seizure activity, loss of consciousness, weakness, visual change, confusion or persistent vomiting with headache should prompt prompt medical assessment [ninds-brain-tumors]. Discuss with a specialist the possibility of a dedicated contrast-enhanced MRI brain-tumour protocol, a thorough clinical examination, specialist review and, where tissue is obtained, histopathological and molecular characterisation, all of which are required for definitive typing and grading under current WHO criteria [who-cns5] [nci-cns-pdq-hp].
